summary: Backend push notifications (Papa en Mousse) validated end-to-end. 15/15 pytest passed covering: (1) GET /api/admin/push-alerts/vapid-key public, returns 87-char key starting with BI55; (2) /summary requires admin (401 without), returns 7 categories with proper schema when admin; (3) POST /subscribe admin-gated, 400 on incomplete, upsert-by-endpoint (no duplicate); (4) DELETE /subscribe removes device; (5) validate/reject on listing (QA-seeded) updates status ('active'/'rejected') and removes from summary; (6) unknown alert_type -> 400; (7) VAPID env-priority: _get_vapid_private_key() returns env value (43 base64url chars); (8) pywebpush signature accepted by real FCM against fake endpoint (410 Gone response — proves the signature/keys are valid, not a serialization error); (9) Robustness: a corrupt subscription in the collection does NOT crash send_push_to_all_admins, and subsequent good subs are still processed (verified via 410 → purge of good sub). Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_push_alerts.py, JUnit: /app/test_reports/pytest/push_alerts.xml. QA-seeded data cleaned up (teardown_module).

minor.issue: Corrupt subscription (invalid p256dh) raises WebPushException with response=None, not ValueError. Current code only purges WebPushException when response.status_code in (404,410) and only purges via `except ValueError` for corrupt keys. Result: corrupt sub is logged & skipped (loop safe), but NOT purged from admin_push_subscriptions, so it will keep triggering warnings every 60s scheduler tick until manually cleaned. Suggest widening purge: `if isinstance(e, WebPushException) and (e.response is None or e.response.status_code in (400,404,410)): delete_one(...)` OR always purge on WebPushException with response None (invalid encryption keys).

action_items: OPTIONAL/minor: In push_service.send_push_to_all_admins, purge subscriptions when WebPushException has response=None (invalid p256dh / corrupt encryption keys). Currently corrupt subs accumulate log noise every scheduler cycle without being auto-cleaned.
critical_code_review_comments: push_service._get_vapid_private_key() correctly prioritizes VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY env over PEM file — VPS deployment fix confirmed working (env value has expected 43 base64url chars).

send_push_to_all_admins now wraps each webpush() in try/except WebPushException + ValueError + generic Exception → loop is genuinely robust (one bad sub does not block the others). Verified experimentally.
push_alerts.py routes are all admin-gated (Depends(admin_only)) except /vapid-key which is intentionally public. Correct.
subscribe uses upsert by endpoint — no duplicates possible. Confirmed via DB count.
validate/reject correctly update the source collections and the item disappears from /summary immediately (no caching). Good.
Minor purge gap noted above under backend_issues.minor — not blocking.
seed_data_creation: QA-PUSH-* listings + fake FCM subscriptions created transiently and cleaned via teardown_module (delete_many with regex ^QA-PUSH-).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Push notification backend fully covered. If main agent later widens the corrupt-sub purge (WebPushException with response=None), update the corresponding assertion in TestSendPushRobustness to check n_corrupt == 0 as well. Real Web Push delivery to a browser cannot be automated — signature validation via fake FCM endpoint is the substitute.
rca of the issue: Not a bug fix iteration — this is verification of the VPS fix (moving VAPID private key from gitignored PEM to VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY env var) and of the newly added robustness (try/except around webpush loop). Both fixes are correctly implemented and verified. Only a minor secondary robustness gap remains: corrupt subs are not auto-purged (only logged).
